name: Rallis India Ltd
title: Rallis India Ltd - 500355 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Rallis Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6% to ₹456 cr and EBITDA moved to ₹-1 cr from ₹-19 cr; management expects 15-25% input cost inflation to be passed on.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹456 cr (up ~6% YoY), with volume growth of ~5% and pricing up ~1%. EBITDA improved to ₹-1 cr from ₹-19 cr and PAT to ₹-15 cr from ₹-32 cr, helped by better B2B exports, CSM and seeds margins. Management described a choppy year (early monsoon, post-September rain gap, short Rabi) and a shift in the industry toward a seller's market after the Middle East conflict. Management is passing through cost increases, calling 15-25% input cost inflation a reality for Kharif, and is guiding to seeds growth in the mid-teens.

financial_highlights.change: improved 96% vs ₹-19 cr in Q4 FY25
vs ₹-32 cr in Q4 FY25 (management cites 52% improvement)

financial_highlights.value: ₹3 cr profit on sale of Aurangabad land

segments.name: Domestic B2C
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹255 cr, up 15% from ₹222 cr on 14% volume growth, led by insecticides. FY26 B2C revenue ₹1,657 cr (+5%, 9% volume growth). Management cites FY26 herbicide +15%, fungicide +5%, insecticide -3%.

segments.name: Soil & Plant Health (within B2C)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹47 cr, up 27% from ₹37 cr on 29% volume growth, driven by micronutrients and biofertilisers. Management says SPH is roughly 20% of B2C sales.

segments.name: Seeds
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹31 cr, up 23% from ₹25 cr (8% volume, 15% price), led by cotton and millets. FY26 seeds revenue ₹481 cr (+15%).

segments.name: Exports (B2B)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹77 cr, down 33% from ₹114 cr on lower Metribuzin and Pendimethalin volumes. Management says Acephate supply is constrained because raw material suppliers compete in US markets.

segments.name: CSM (contract manufacturing)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹66 cr, up 59% from ₹41 cr on both volume and price. Margin was helped by a contract clause that pays benefit if volumes fall below thresholds.

segments.name: B2B total
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹170 cr, down 7%; FY26 B2B revenue ₹759 cr (+14%) on volume, price and customer base growth.

guidance_outlook: Seeds: management expects high double-digit growth in FY27 on a combination of price and volume, clarified as mid-teens; cotton expected to grow fastest, then maize, rice and millet.
Crop protection: price increases of roughly 5-10% expected; revenue growth could be double-digit; margins described as stable to soft depending on competitor response.
Input costs have risen 15-25%; management says this is a reality for Kharif and will take 3-4 months to unwind even if the war ends.
Management is not building inventory beyond Kharif and will buy only what it can sell; Kharif raw material is largely secured.
Monsoon forecast at 92% of LPA; management says a total failure is unlikely and planting will happen regardless.
capex_capacity: Record production levels achieved through better manufacturing efficiency; FY26 annual capacity utilisation improved vs FY25.
Five ingredients produced in-house for crop protection; other inputs sourced from suppliers, with Kharif supply secured.
Seeds focus narrowed to five strategic crops: cotton, maize, millet, mustard and rice.
Inventory slightly elevated YoY at quarter end; Rallis built some low-cost raw material inventory ahead of the war.
Aquafeed is at an experimental stage with no investment size set; management wants one more year before deciding. Micronutrient business has reached ₹50 cr+ scale.
demand_pricing: Industry is moving from a buyers' market to a seller's market after the Iran war, with panic buying and hoarding reported. Glyphosate is up ~25%, and Glufosinate, Mancozeb, Metribuzin and other generic AIs have also risen.
Rabi was hit by unseasonal rain and hail on 2.49 lakh ha. Summer sowing is down 4.7% YoY as of end-March.
Management expects the sector to grow 3-4% in FY27 (this figure was later clarified to be GDP growth), with volumes possibly shrinking on lower acreage and margins stable to soft.

Price increases announced early; management sees a price increase on crop protection of 5-10%, with seed pricing rising for rice, maize and millet but flat for cotton (government did not raise cotton prices).
Competitive intensity: Clasto and Benzilla inventory was liquidated in Q4, compressing B2C gross margin on a standalone basis.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement in Q4 when the commentary was pessimistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CSM margins were higher due to a volume-threshold clause and SPH, exports and seeds were better, while standalone crop protection margin fell because of Clasto and Benzilla inventory liquidation in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 B2C volume growth came from pre-placement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said placement was limited to normal levels; some low-cost inventory was held back for Q1 sales at higher prices. For FY26, herbicide was up 15%, fungicide 5% and insecticide down 3%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth and margin outlook for seeds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects high double-digit growth, clarified as mid-teens, from price and volume. Dryer capacity constraints and paddy open-field drying raised costs, so margin outcome is still uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost increases and how much can be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Input costs have risen 15-25%. Management has announced price increases, expects them to hold through Kharif, and says a 3-4 month unwind is needed even if the war ends.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the B2C growth came from SPH and what is core crop protection growth?
qa_highlights.answer: SPH grew 27%; excluding SPH, B2C crop protection growth is marginal, low single digit, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory risk if crude prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not hold excess inventory and is building only Kharif stock, with calibrated purchases to match expected sales.

risks_watch: Monsoon risk: IMD forecasts 92% of LPA with El Niño; management cites 5-10% demand cut risk for herbicides and insecticides under erratic rain.
Input cost inflation of 15-25% may compress downstream margins if prices cannot be passed on fully, and competitors' price responses are unknown.
Acephate export supply constrained by raw material suppliers who compete in US markets; exports fell 33% in Q4.
Seed margin uncertainty from dryer capacity constraints, incremental drying costs and possible lower recovery.
Kharif inventory costing and the state of the Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz remain open items.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on seeds, CSM and SPH and on pricing power, but cautious on crop protection demand, the monsoon and margins. It repeatedly said the outlook is too uncertain to predict, and it gave limited detail on margin guidance, company-level inventory and the B2C split.

growth.why: Seeds guided to high double-digit (mid-teens) FY27 growth from price and volume, and crop protection price hikes of 5-10% support double-digit revenue growth, but no new capacity or firm order book is quantified and the sector is guided to grow only 3-4%.
